newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slump in absence of institutions.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slump in absence of institutions.

text.p: Egyptian shares slumped across the board to a seven-week low on Sunday as small investors pulled out of the market in the expectation that prices will keep falling for a little while longer.
Broker Sherif Cararah said he thought further corrections were possible but the market could rebound in about a month when newly created funds step in with more cash.
"We're in a grey transitional phase. It might go down further but I don't see further severe downs," he said.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said the all-share index fell 1.5 percent or 5.63 points to 373.05, its lowest level since January 30. Volume was 34.34 million pounds ($10.1 million), thinner than on any day since January 12.
After record highs about a month ago, securities house HSBC James Capel forecast the market would stabilise with the all-share index between 370 and 375 points -- its current level.
The average transaction size on Sunday, just over 8,000 pounds each, showed that institutions were not active. But foreign funds are not normally big players on Sundays.
The slump hit all the traditionally dominant sectors -- the millers, cements and banks -- with few exceptions.
Year-end results released by Commercial International Bank (CIB) had no noticeable effect. The shares fell 4.40 pounds to 83.92 despite an 11 percent increase in profits.
In the milling sector, Central and West Delta Flour Mills led the way down, shedding 4.25 pounds to close at 96.25 in trade worth 3.4 million pounds.
Southern Cairo Flour Mills and East Delta Flour Mills both run into the five percent limit for the amount any share can fall in a single session.
Among the big cement companies, only Egyptian Tora Portland Cement held its ground, closing unchanged at 98.00.
Internationally traded Suez Cement lost 0.75 to end the day at 68.50 pounds.
Misr International Bank/MIBANK and rarely traded Housing and Development Bank were two of the few high-volume shares which gained in Sunday's session.

The housing bank traded in large blocks, possibly as part of the government's programme for public-sector banks to sell off their shares in such joint-venture banks, and it closed 1.48 pounds up at 124.00, an all-time high.
MIBANK gained 3.50 to 700 in active trading.
The index for openly traded firms fell sharply, to 578.74 from 594.44 on Thursday, and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 257.58 from 259.44 points.
Out of the 81 shares traded, 14 gained, 30 lost and 37 ended the day unchanged.
